body: It seems to be working when I set the template as an inner class (and even just by renaming Templates folder in templates), but what is disturbing is the different behaviour in dev and in prod. I expect the build to fail if the folder name is not good !

I've tried the attached reproducer and the build fails correctly on Linux because your project declares the templates in the `src/main/resources/Templates` directory, but it should be `src/main/resources/templates`; as a result no templates are found. When I fix the directory name to `templates` everything seems to work fine. The question is why the build did not fail on Windows...

> I expect the build to fail if the folder name is not good !

Yes, it should fail and it fails on Linux...
is File::exist case insensitive on windows ?

~I don't think that we use `File#exists()` in the build steps.~ Ah, you mean the one used in `io.quarkus.bootstrap.model.PathsCollection.resolveExistingOrNull(String)`...

Anyway, could you pls try to enable the debug logging for qute so that we have a little bit more info? Just add the `quarkus.log.category."io.quarkus.qute.deployment".level=DEBUG` to your `application.properties`.

So my guess is that `ApplicationArchive.getChildPath(String)` returns the path `src/main/resources/Templates` for the parameter `templates`, i.e. is case-insensitive on Windows. Then we collect all templates and build the relevant metadata. However, at runtime the [EngineProducer](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/extensions/qute/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/qute/runtime/EngineProducer.java#L195) expects a template to be located in the `templates` directory and `java.lang.ClassLoader.getResource(String)` is case-sensitive.

issue.title: Qute template scanning - fix case-insensitivity problem on Windows
